newsitem.title: FRANCE: Credit National jumps on bid speculation.
newsitem.headline: Credit National jumps on bid speculation.

text.p: French bank Credit National shares jumped by 7.50 percent on Wednesday on renewed market speculation it could become a bid target.

But banking analysts were at a loss to suggest potential buyers and Credit National said on Wednesday it was not aware of plans by any of its long-term shareholders which own a combined 31 percent of the bank to sell their stakes.
Shares in Credit National closed up 21.20 francs at 303.80 francs. The shares rose 1.7 percent on Tuesday.
Emmanuel Rodocanachi, chairman of Credit National which has been declaring for some time its shares were undervalued, said last month it was "without a doubt a tempting target".
Wednesday's buying was fuelled by a report in the financial daily La Tribune which said banks BNP, Credit Commercial de France or Caisses d'Epargne might be interested in Credit National.
The paper said the bank's stock was undervalued and it had a re-evaluated net asset worth of between 500 to 550 francs per share. The bank has said it thinks its shares are worth 600 francs.
"This is the second time this fall we've had this kind of bid speculation," said one banking analyst.

"It makes sense Credit National should be a takeover target as its share is trading below book value and it has three billion francs worth of shareholders funds," he said. But "it doesn't make sense BNP, the Caisses d'Epargne or CCF or would want to extend their activities in that fashion."
Analysts said even though its shares were undervalued, weak investment returns and worries about its core business lending activities, plagued by weak demand, made the bank less attractive.

The bank's credit ratings were recently downgraded after it plunged to a half year loss of 112 million francs ($21 million) compared with a profit of 236 million francs ($45 million) for the year-earlier period.
The loss reflected a restructuring charge to cover its merger with French bank Banque Francaise de Commerce Exterieur.
Credit National's shares have been recovering after falling to a year low of 226 francs on the back of the results.
The bank's long-term shareholders are insurer Axa, with 9.5 percent, state-owned Caisse des Depots et Consignations with seven percent and AGF with seven percent.
Credit Foncier de France owns 2.5 percent and Germany's IKB holds five percent. Insurer UAP which is merging with Axa but which is not part of the shareholders' pact, holds 3.5 percent.
